arxiv-2002-02914.title: Improving the GP 2 Compiler
arxiv-2002-02914.creator: Graham Campbell ​, Jack Romo ​, Detlef Plump ​
arxiv-2002-02914.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Graham Campbell ​, Jack Romo ​, Detlef Plump ​. GP 2 is an experimental programming language based on graph transformation rules which aims to facilitate program analysis and verification. Writing efficient programs in such a language is hard because graph matching is expensive, however GP 2 addresses this problem by providing rooted rules which, under mild conditions, can be matched in constant time using the GP 2 to C compiler.

arxiv-2012-13591.title: Spin-circuit representation of spin-torque ferromagnetic resonance
arxiv-2012-13591.creator: Kuntal Roy
arxiv-2012-13591.description: Abstract Spin-torque ferromagnetic resonance (ST-FMR) particularly using magnetic insulators and heavy metals possessing a giant spin Hall effect (SHE) has gotten a lot of attention for the development of spintronic devices. To devise complex functional devices, it is necessary to construct the equivalent spin-circuit representations of different phenomena.

arxiv-2012-14305.title: Adaptive Threshold for Online Object Recognition and Re-identification Tasks
arxiv-2012-14305.creator: Bharat Bohara
arxiv-2012-14305.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Bharat Bohara. Choosing a decision threshold is one of the challenging job in any classification tasks. How much the model is accurate, if the deciding boundary is not picked up carefully, its entire performance would go in vain. On the other hand, for imbalance classification where one of the classes is dominant over another, relying on the conventional method of choosing threshold would result in poor performance.

arxiv-2201-11982.title: Hydrodynamic behavior of the 2–TASEP
arxiv-2201-11982.creator: Ali Zahra
arxiv-2201-11982.description: Abstract We address the question of the large scale or hydrodynamic behavior of a 2-species generalization of TASEP (2–TASEP), consisting of two kinds of particles, moving in opposite directions and swapping their positions. We compute the rarefaction and shock solutions of the hydrodynamic equations of the model, showing that these equations form a Temple class system.

arxiv-2211-09867.title: Response to ‘Comment on “Quantum correlations are weaved by the spinors of the Euclidean primitives”’
arxiv-2211-09867.creator: Joy Christian
arxiv-2211-09867.description: Abstract In this paper I respond to a critique of one of my papers previously published in the Royal Society Open Science entitled “Quantum correlations are weaved by the spinors of the Euclidean primitives.” Without engaging with the geometrical framework presented in my paper, the critique incorrectly claims that there are mathematical errors in it.

arxiv-2406-19460.description: Abstract Type Ia supernova (SN Ia) light curves have a secondary maximum that exists in the r r , i i , and near-infrared filters. The secondary maximum is relatively weak in the r r band, but holds the advantage that it is accessible, even at high redshift.

arxiv-2503-03940.title: Passive Sonar Sensor Placement for Undersea Surveillance
arxiv-2503-03940.creator: Graham V. Weinberg, Martijn van der Merwe
arxiv-2503-03940.description: Abstract Detection of undersea threats is a complex problem of considerable importance for maritime regional surveillance and security. Multistatic sonar systems can provide a means to monitor for underwater threats, where fixed sensors, towed arrays and dipping sonars may be utilised for this purpose. However, it is advantageous to deploy passive sensors to provide a stealthy early warning system.

arxiv-2503-22619.title: Contact diagrams for chords
arxiv-2503-22619.creator: Yiyang Jia
arxiv-2503-22619.description: Abstract We demonstrate how contact chord diagrams can arise from certain Fock-space models and compute the corresponding correlation functions using the chord path integral technique. In particular, our three-point functions are in the right form dictated by conformal symmetry, and some of our four-point functions match the results of some AdS 2 contact Witten diagrams.

arxiv-2509-15794.title: Bridging Batch and Streaming Estimations to System Identification under Adversarial Attacks
arxiv-2509-15794.creator: Jihun Kim, Javad Lavaei
arxiv-2509-15794.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Jihun Kim, Javad Lavaei. System identification in modern engineering systems faces emerging challenges from unanticipated adversarial attacks beyond existing detection mechanisms. In this work, we obtain a provably accurate estimate of the Markov parameter matrix of order k k to identify partially observed linear systems, in which the probability of having an attack at each time is O ⁡ ( 1 / k ) O(1/k) .

arxiv-2510-13769.title: Optical Response of Graphene Quantum Dots in the Visible Spectrum: A Combined DFT-QED Approach
arxiv-2510-13769.creator: J. Olivo
arxiv-2510-13769.description: Abstract Abstract We propose a model based on density functional theory (DFT) and quantum electrodynamics (QED) to study the dynamical characteristics of graphene quantum dots (GQDs). We assume the GQD edges are saturated with hydrogen atoms, effectively making it a polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) such as coronene.

arxiv-2601-00294.title: Bridging Commutant and Polynomial Methods for Hilbert Space Fragmentation
arxiv-2601-00294.creator: Bo-Ting Chen, Yu-Ping Wang, Biao Lian
arxiv-2601-00294.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Bo-Ting Chen, Yu-Ping Wang, Biao Lian. A quantum model exhibits Hilbert space fragmentation (HSF) if its Hilbert space decomposes into exponentially many dynamically disconnected subspaces, known as Krylov subspaces. A model may however have different HSFs depending on the method for identifying them. Here we establish a connection between two vastly distinct methods recently proposed for identifying HSF: the commutant algebra (CA) method and integer characteristic polynomial factorization (ICPF) method.

pmc-10648974.title: Oral and Topical Administration of a Standardized Saw Palmetto Oil Reduces Hair Fall and Improves the Hair Growth in Androgenetic Alopecia Subjects – A 16-Week Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Study
pmc-10648974.creator: Heggar Venkataramana Sudeep, Sriram Rashmi, Thomas V Jestin, Aleksander Richards, Kuluvar Gouthamchandra, Kodimule Shyamprasad
pmc-10648974.description: PurposeAndrogenetic alopecia (AGA) is the most common type of hair loss in humans, affecting self-esteem and emotional well-being. This study aimed to assess the safety and efficacy of VISPOTM, a standardized saw palmetto oil (2–3% β-sitosterol), in subjects with mild-to-moderate AGA.

pmc-12626143.title: Hysteroscopy as an Alternative to Curettage in Persistent Pregnancy of Unknown Location
pmc-12626143.creator: Ishai Levin, Aviad Cohen, Yael Shulman, Yossi Tsur, Yaron Gil, Shikma Bar-On
pmc-12626143.description: This study evaluates the effectiveness of hysteroscopy in managing persistent pregnancy of unknown location (PUL) as an alternative to traditional curettage. Six patients diagnosed with PUL underwent hysteroscopy, four of them by the vaginoscopic approach and without anesthesia, and two under general anesthesia.

pmc-12664592.title: Impact of Age and Sex on Coronary Flow Reserve and Microvascular Function in Patients With Angina and Nonobstructive Coronary Arteries
pmc-12664592.creator: Spyridon Kostantinis, Gabriel Garcia Castro, Nida Latif, Natasha Cigarroa, Steffne J Kunnirickal, Natalija Odanovic, Samit M Shah
pmc-12664592.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundAngina and nonobstructive coronary arteries is increasingly recognized, but the impact of age and sex on coronary microvascular function in this population has received limited study.MethodsIn 206 consecutive patients with angina and nonobstructive coronary arteries, invasive coronary function testing was performed including vasoreactivity testing with acetylcholine provocation, guidewire–based assessment of coronary flow reserve (CFR) with bolus thermodilution, and index of microcirculatory resistance (IMR).

pmc-13145984.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A642 USE OF KNEE IMMOBILISERS TO REDUCE POST-THROMBECTOMY FEMORAL ACCESS SITE COMPLICATIONS
pmc-13145984.creator: Christopher Gilbert, Jason Schick, Muhammad Farooq, Kasim Qureshi
pmc-13145984.description: Background and aimsEndovascular thrombectomy is the standard of care for patients presenting with an acute large vessel occlusion stroke who meet inclusion criteria. Femoral access site complications are common due to ipsilateral leg movement post-procedure leading to reopening of the arterial puncture site. There is lack of data regarding the optimal type of post-procedural limb immobilisation.

pmc-13150670.title: Efficacy of Upadacitinib in a Middle‐Aged Man With Netherton Syndrome Refractory to Dupilumab: A Case Report
pmc-13150670.creator: Bo‐Jie Yu, Pei‐Ling Li, Bing‐Sian Lin, Shou‐En Wu, Chih‐Tsung Hung
pmc-13150670.description: 51‐year‐old Han Chinese man with a lifelong history of atopic dermatitis (AD) had failed multiple treatments, including topical corticosteroids, oral cyclosporine, methotrexate, and phototherapy (Figure 1a). Given limited efficacy and high serum immunoglobulin‐E (IgE) (1759 IU/mL), he began dupilumab (600 mg loading dose, then 300 mg every 2 weeks).

pmc-13315125.title: Clinical Care and Referral Pathways for Food Security Screening in Health Care: A Scoping Review
pmc-13315125.creator: Sydney Yearley, Ronit Ridberg, Allie Tatarian, Lizbeth Moreno Loaeza, Saverio Feudo, Saahil Patel, Molly Duncan, Dariush Mozaffarian
pmc-13315125.description: BackgroundFood and nutrition insecurity are linked to poor health outcomes and disparities, yet how health care systems implement screening and referrals remains poorly understood.MethodsWe searched for studies evaluating screening and referral processes for food and nutrition insecurity for patients of all ages in US health care settings.

pmc-13407655.title: Exploratory Associations of Personality Traits, Cognitive Emotion Regulation, and Quality of Life with DSM-Related Symptom Burden in Gambling Disorder
pmc-13407655.creator: Ioana Ioniță, Mădălina Iuliana Mușat, Bogdan Cătălin, Dan Adrian Lutescu, Constantin Alexandru Ciobanu, Adela Magdalena Ciobanu

This exploratory cross-sectional study examined associations between DSM-5-TR symptom burden, personality dimensions, cognitive emotion regulation, quality of life, and sociodemographic variables in a Romanian clinical sample. pmc-13544011.title: Diazepam-Associated Hypotension Contributing to Recurrent Syncope in an Older Adult
pmc-13544011.creator: Manar Shalak, Nafiisah Rajabalee, Harsha Sai Sreemantula,
pmc-13544011.description: Syncope in older adults is often multifactorial, with polypharmacy being a common and potentially modifiable factor. Benzodiazepines are prescribed for anxiety and insomnia in this population despite being associated with adverse effects, including falls, cognitive impairment, and hypotension.We present the case of a 68-year-old female patient with multimorbidity and recurrent unexplained syncope despite extensive cardiologic and neurologic evaluations.
